feedback.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{3x-{x}^{2}}{5{x}^{4}-4}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3x-{x}^{2}}{5{x}^{4}-4} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3x}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{5{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(5-\frac{4}{{x}^{4}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{3}{{x}^{3}},\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$ and $\frac{4}{{x}^{4}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(5-\frac{4}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & \to \frac{0-0}{5-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
